purpose: attribution index for the developer gap analysis: step shape -> FHIR feature -> supplying FHIR package -> IRIS subsystem

UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION.signal: a FHIR operation ($book, $update-metadata) is invoked or declared and the SUT does not implement it
UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION.irisLocus: the endpoint's OperationHandlerClass. Built-in operations resolve to FHIR<Scope>Op<Name> methods on HS.FHIRServer.Storage.BuiltInOperations; a custom operation needs a subclass of it plus an InteractionsStrategy subclass, installed before the endpoint is created.

PROFILE_NONCONFORMANCE.signal: the response body does not satisfy an ISiK StructureDefinition - either a profile validation step or a FHIRPath assertion over an element the profile marks mustSupport
PROFILE_NONCONFORMANCE.irisLocus: resource content, not IRIS code, in most cases: the SUT returns what was stored. Read the quoted validator message first. IRIS code is implicated when the element was stored and is missing from the response (JSON/XML export in HS.FHIRServer.Util.* or the storage strategy's ToJSON path).

MISSING_SEARCH_PARAM.signal: a search parameter the ISiK CapabilityStatement requires is absent from the SUT's CapabilityStatement, or a search using it does not filter
MISSING_SEARCH_PARAM.irisLocus: search-parameter indexing. The endpoint's SearchParameter set comes from the packages loaded by HS.FHIRMeta.Load.NpmLoader and selected in the instance's package list; an unindexed parameter is not advertised.

CAPABILITY_STATEMENT_GAP.signal: the SUT's generated CapabilityStatement omits an interaction, resource type or operation the ISiK conformance resource declares as SHALL
CAPABILITY_STATEMENT_GAP.irisLocus: CapabilityStatement generation. IRIS builds /metadata from the endpoint's package set and strategy capabilities; a missing entry means the resource type or interaction is not enabled on the endpoint rather than merely undeclared.

SEARCH_SEMANTICS.signal: a search executes but returns the wrong set - a modifier, prefix, chain, _include or paging behaviour is not honoured
SEARCH_SEMANTICS.irisLocus: the search layer: modifier and prefix handling in the strategy's search implementation, and the SearchQueryProcessor for chained and reverse-chained parameters.

RESPONSE_FORMAT.signal: the REST envelope is wrong rather than the resource: content type, charset, _format, HTTP status, or the identity of what a read returned
RESPONSE_FORMAT.irisLocus: the REST layer - content negotiation and the read path in HS.FHIRServer.Service / the interactions strategy. Note this category deliberately also covers `resource has ID` assertions: they check that a read of /Type/{id} echoes that logical id, which is the same code path.

REFERENCE_INTEGRITY.signal: a Reference.reference does not resolve to the expected resource, or a referenced resource is missing from a bundle the SUT assembled
REFERENCE_INTEGRITY.irisLocus: reference storage and rewriting: how the strategy persists Reference.reference and what _include / revinclude assembles into a search bundle.

WRITE_VALIDATION_GAP.signal: a write the ISiK profile forbids was accepted, or one it requires was refused - the status code disagrees with the profile, whatever the stored resource then contains
WRITE_VALIDATION_GAP.irisLocus: the write path's validation depth: the interactions strategy's Add/Update path and what it does with the endpoint's configured ResourceValidation setting. $validate is a separate code path and a result there does not settle this one. Which schema this build's write path actually enforces is a measurement on a running SUT, so this index - written at `make packages` time, with no SUT reachable - does not state it: take the two-request probe in docs/en/07-reports.md against the round's own endpoint and record the result beside the round.

AUTHORIZATION_SCOPE.signal: a request carrying a SMART-on-FHIR access token was answered with resources outside the scope that token grants, or the SMART discovery document is absent or incomplete - the Connect module, added by test suite release 3.0.0
AUTHORIZATION_SCOPE.irisLocus: the endpoint's OAuth 2.0 configuration and the authorization it delegates to. An IRIS FHIR endpoint answers /.well-known/smart-configuration with <HSFHIRErr>NoOAuth2Handling until an OAuth 2.0 client is configured on it, so scope enforcement is a deployment property of the endpoint and not of the FHIR layer alone.

ENVIRONMENT_PREREQUISITE.signal: the scenario's own precondition was not met by this test environment, so the case states nothing about the SUT. Established from positive evidence in the official report only - see index['prerequisiteRules']
ENVIRONMENT_PREREQUISITE.irisLocus: none. This is a property of the deployment this round used, not of the product. Excluded from the gap count for the same reason TEST_DATA_DEFECT is: a count that mixes in cases whose precondition failed overstates the work.

UPSTREAM_SUITE_CONFLICT.signal: the case failed on the suite rather than on the response, in one of two ways, each established from positive evidence only. Either two steps require incompatible things of the same body, so no response can satisfy both - the rejected content is content the suite's own feature files require, see index['suiteRequiredCrossVersionExtensions'] - or the step raised a NullPointerException inside the suite's own evaluation, naming the suite library method whose return value it dereferenced, so it never compared an expectation against the response at all
UPSTREAM_SUITE_CONFLICT.irisLocus: none. This is a defect in the test suite, not in the product and not in this project's test data. Each entry states which of the two kinds it is; where it is a crash, read the exchange anyway, because a response the suite could not evaluate is not thereby a correct one. The first measured instance of the incompatible-requirements kind is the R5 cross-version extension set: a Stufe 5 feature asserts `extension.where(url = 'http://hl7.org/fhir/5.0/StructureDefinition/extension-Encounter.plannedStartDate').exists()` and the ISiK package defines that extension, while a later step validates the enclosing Bundle against core FHIR R4, which rejects any 5.0 extension URL as an invalid version. Excluded from the gap count for the same reason the two categories below are.

TEST_DATA_DEFECT.signal: the seeded resource was absent, unreadable or already flagged by $validate before the run, or the content the reference validator rejected is the content this project staged - so the failure is ours, not the SUT's
TEST_DATA_DEFECT.irisLocus: none. This is a defect in this project's test data or seeding, proven from provenance/seed/*.json or from the staged instances in provenance/corpus/, and is reported in a separate appendix so it cannot inflate the IRIS gap count.

UNCLASSIFIED.signal: the failing step's shape is not in this index's classification table - almost always a test suite version that grew a new step shape
UNCLASSIFIED.irisLocus: unknown. The entry quotes the step and the response verbatim so it is still actionable, and build_index.py reports the unclassified shape so the table can be extended.

irisLociProvenance: Authored by this project, not derived from any artefact. No file in this repository maps a FHIR feature to an IRIS class; these are the subsystems an IRIS for Health developer would open, stated so the gap report can point somewhere. Verify against the product source before acting on one.

statusRules.when: the request path contains /$ and the status is 404 or 400
statusRules.why: IRIS answers an unknown operation with 404 and an OperationOutcome; 400 is the same gap reported as a bad request

statusRules.when: the status is 404 on a plain /Type/{id} read
statusRules.why: the resource the scenario needs is not in the SUT. Confirmed against provenance/seed/<Level>.json before being reported as ours

statusRules.when: the status is 404 or 405 on a write to /Type
statusRules.why: the endpoint does not accept that interaction on that resource type

statusRules.when: the status is 400 or 422 on a write
statusRules.why: the SUT rejected the body; the OperationOutcome names the constraint

statusRules.when: the assertion targets $.header.* or a contentType
statusRules.why: content negotiation, independent of the resource content

statusRules.when: the assertion targets $.responseCode and no other rule applied
statusRules.why: the status line is the REST envelope

responseCodeRules.when: the suite demanded 4xx or 422 and the SUT answered 2xx
responseCodeRules.why: the write was accepted although the profile the suite validated against forbids the body. What the write path did validate against is not established by this case - see the category's irisLocus

responseCodeRules.when: the suite demanded 2xx and the SUT answered 400
responseCodeRules.why: the mirror image: a body ISiK requires the SUT to accept was rejected. Same code path, opposite direction, so the same locus

responseCodeRules.when: the suite demanded 422 and the SUT answered 400
responseCodeRules.why: both are rejections, so the SUT did detect the defect; FHIR reserves 422 for a body that is well-formed but fails validation and 400 for one that is malformed. The distinction is in the REST layer's error mapping, but the decision that produced it is the write path's, which is why this is not RESPONSE_FORMAT

responseCodeRules.when: the SUT answered 5xx to any expected status
responseCodeRules.why: an unhandled server error is not a conformance verdict; the quoted body and the SUT's own log are the evidence

responseBodyRules.when: the failure is scenario-scope and its message is the suite's own "CapabilityStatement-Definition for search parameter 'p' of resource 'R' is either missing or incorrect"
responseBodyRules.why: the suite's FhirPathValidation raised this instead of a step assertion, so no step shape is available - but the message names the parameter and the resource, which is the whole finding. Measured: 1 occurrence, combo-code-value-quantity on Observation

responseBodyRules.when: a FHIRPath assertion failed with HAPI-1857 (no content to parse) after a write
responseBodyRules.why: the SUT returned no body on create, so there was nothing to assert over. IRIS withholds the created resource unless the request carries Prefer: return=representation; the suite sends no Prefer header and ISiK expects the resource or a Parameters. The locus is the interactions strategy's create path and its default return preference - there is no endpoint configuration for it (HS.FHIRServer.API.ConfigData carries DefaultPreferHandling, which governs unknown *search parameters*, and no return-preference property), so the default is decided in code

prerequisiteRules.when: the request the failing assertion was made about carries an Authorization header whose value is still the suite's own SET-YOUR-TOKEN-HERE placeholder
prerequisiteRules.why: the scenario's stated precondition is a valid Bearer token for a named scope. No token was issued, so no scope was presented, so nothing was asserted about the SUT's scope enforcement

prerequisiteRules.when: the request is for /.well-known/smart-configuration AND the same run shows unresolved token placeholders elsewhere
prerequisiteRules.why: that path is the SMART-on-FHIR authorization discovery document, which describes an authorization server. The placeholders are this run's own evidence that none was configured. The second condition is what keeps the rule from excusing a genuine discovery defect in a round that did supply tokens
